verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你告诉亚伦子孙作祭司的说：祭司不可为民中的死人沾染自己，
verses.en: The Lord said to Moses, “Say to the priests, the sons of Aaron—say to them: ‘For a dead person[NOTE:1] no priest[NOTE:2] is to defile himself among his people,[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “soul, person, life”) can sometimes refer to a “dead person” (cf. Lev 19:28 above and the literature cited there).

Heb “no one,” but “priest” has been used in the translation to clarify that these restrictions are limited to the priests, not to the Israelites in general (note the introductory formula, “say to the priests, the sons of Aaron”).
The MT has “in his peoples,” but Smr, LXX, Syriac, Targum, and Tg. Ps.-J. have “in his people,” referring to the Israelites as a whole.

verses.zh: 除非为他骨肉之亲的父母、儿女、弟兄，
verses.en: except for his close relative who is near to him[NOTE:1]—his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
notes: Heb “except for his flesh, the one near to him.”

verses.zh: 和未曾出嫁、作处女的姊妹，才可以沾染自己。
verses.en: and his virgin sister who is near to him,[NOTE:1] who has no husband—he may defile himself for her.
notes: Cf. v. 2a.

verses.zh: 祭司既在民中为首，就不可从俗沾染自己。
verses.en: He must not defile himself as a husband among his people so as to profane himself.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “He shall not defile himself a husband in his peoples, to profane himself.” The meaning of the line is disputed, but it appears to prohibit a priest from burying any relative by marriage (as opposed to the blood relatives of vv. 2-3), including his wife (compare B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 142-43 with J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 343, 348).

verses.zh: 不可使头光秃；不可剃除胡须的周围，也不可用刀划身。
verses.en: Priests[NOTE:1] must not have a bald spot shaved on their head, they must not shave the corner of their beard, and they must not cut slashes in their body.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (priests, see the beginning of v. 1) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and in their body they shall not [cut] slash[es]” (cf. Lev 19:28). The context connects these sorts of mutilations with mourning rites (cf. Lev 19:27-28 above).

verses.zh: 要归　神为圣，不可亵渎　神的名；因为耶和华的火祭，就是　神的食物，是他们献的，所以他们要成为圣。
verses.en: “‘They must be holy to their God, and they must not profane[NOTE:1] the name of their God, because they are the ones who present the Lord’s gifts,[NOTE:2] the food of their God. Therefore they must be holy.[NOTE:3]
notes: Regarding “profane,” see the note on Lev 10:10 above.
Regarding the Hebrew term for “gifts,” see the note on Lev 1:9 above (cf. also 3:11 and 16 in combination with the word for “food” that follows in the next phrase here).
Smr and all early versions have the plural adjective “holy” rather than the MT singular noun “holiness.”

verses.zh: 不可娶妓女或被污的女人为妻，也不可娶被休的妇人为妻，因为祭司是归　神为圣。
verses.en: They must not take a wife defiled by prostitution,[NOTE:1] nor are they to take a wife divorced from her husband,[NOTE:2] for the priest[NOTE:3] is holy to his God.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “A wife harlot and profaned they shall not take.” The structure of the verse (e.g., “wife” at the beginning of the two main clauses) suggests that “harlot and profaned” constitutes a hendiadys, meaning “a wife defiled by harlotry” (see the explanation in B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 143, as opposed to that in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 343, 348; cf. v. 14 below). Cf. NASB “a woman who is profaned by harlotry.”
For a helpful discussion of divorce in general and as it relates to this passage see B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 143-44.
Heb “he”; the referent (the priest) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The pronoun “he” in this clause refers to the priest, not the former husband of the divorced woman.

verses.zh: 所以你要使他成圣，因为他奉献你　神的食物；你要以他为圣，因为我―使你们成圣的耶和华―是圣的。
verses.en: You must sanctify him because he presents the food of your God. He must be holy to you because I, the Lord who sanctifies you all,[NOTE:1] am holy.
notes: The three previous second person references in this verse are all singular, but this reference is plural. By adding “all” this grammatical distinction is preserved in the translation.

verses.zh: 祭司的女儿若行淫辱没自己，就辱没了父亲，必用火将她焚烧。
verses.en: If a daughter of a priest profanes herself by engaging in prostitution, she is profaning her father. She must be burned to death.[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on “burned to death” in 20:14.

verses.zh: 「在弟兄中作大祭司、头上倒了膏油、又承接圣职，穿了圣衣的，不可蓬头散发，也不可撕裂衣服。
verses.en: “‘The high[NOTE:1] priest—who is greater than his brothers, and on whose head the anointing oil is poured, and who has been ordained[NOTE:2] to wear the priestly garments—must neither dishevel the hair of his head nor tear his garments.[NOTE:3]
notes: The adjective “high” has been supplied in the translation for clarity, as in many English versions.
Heb “and he has filled his hand.” For this expression see the note on Lev 8:33.

Regarding these signs of mourning see the note on Lev 10:6. His head had been anointed (v. 10a) so it must not be unkempt (v. 10b), and his garments were special priestly garments (v. 10a) so he must not tear them (v. 10b). In the translation “garments” has been employed rather than “clothes” to suggest that the special priestly garments are referred to here; cf. NRSV “nor tear his vestments.”

verses.zh: 不可挨近死尸，也不可为父母沾染自己。
verses.en: He must not go where there is any dead person;[NOTE:1] he must not defile himself even for his father or for his mother.
notes: Although the MT has “persons” (plural), the LXX and Syriac have the singular “person” corresponding to the singular adjectival participle “dead” (cf. also Num 6:6).

verses.zh: 不可出圣所，也不可亵渎　神的圣所，因为　神膏油的冠冕在他头上。我是耶和华。
verses.en: He must not go out from the sanctuary and must not profane[NOTE:1] the sanctuary of his God, because the dedication of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the Lord.
notes: Regarding “profane,” see the note on Lev 10:10 above.

verses.zh: 他要娶处女为妻。
verses.en: He must take a wife who is a virgin.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And he, a wife in her virginity he shall take.”

verses.zh: 寡妇或是被休的妇人，或是被污为妓的女人，都不可娶；只可娶本民中的处女为妻。
verses.en: He must not marry[NOTE:1] a widow, a divorced woman, or one profaned by prostitution; he may only take a virgin from his people[NOTE:2] as a wife,
notes: Heb “take.” In context this means “take as wife,” i.e., “marry.”
The MT has literally, “from his peoples,” but Smr, LXX, Syriac, Targum, and Tg. Ps.-J. have “from his people,” referring to the Israelites as a whole.

verses.zh: 不可在民中辱没他的儿女，因为我是叫他成圣的耶和华。」
verses.en: so that he does not profane his children among his people,[NOTE:1] for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.’”
notes: The MT has literally, “in his peoples,” but Smr, LXX, Syriac, Targum, and Tg. Ps.-J. have “in his people,” referring to the Israelites as a whole.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你告诉亚伦说：你世世代代的后裔，凡有残疾的，都不可近前来献他　神的食物。
verses.en: “Tell Aaron, ‘No man from your descendants throughout their generations[NOTE:1] who has a physical flaw[NOTE:2] is to approach to present the food of his God.
notes: Heb “to their generations.”

Heb “who in him is a flaw”; cf. KJV, ASV “any blemish”; NASB, NIV “a defect.” The rendering “physical flaw” is used to refer to any birth defect or physical injury of the kind described in the following verses (cf. the same Hebrew word also in Lev 24:19-20). The same term is used for “flawed” animals, which must not be offered to the Lord in Lev 22:20-25.

verses.zh: 因为凡有残疾的，无论是瞎眼的、瘸腿的、塌鼻子的、肢体有余的、
verses.en: Certainly[NOTE:1] no man who has a physical flaw is to approach: a blind man, or one who is lame, or one with a slit nose,[NOTE:2] or who has a limb too long,
notes: The particle כִּי (ki) in this context is asseverative, indicating absolutely certainty (GKC 498 §159.ee).

Lexically, the Hebrew term חָרֻם (kharum) seems to refer to a split nose or perhaps any number of other facial defects (HALOT 354 s.v. II חרם qal; cf. G. J. Wenham, Leviticus [NICOT], 292, n. 7); cf. KJV, ASV “a flat nose”; NASB “a disfigured face.” The NJPS translation is “a limb too short” as a balance to the following term which means “extended, raised,” and apparently refers to “a limb too long” (see the explanation in B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 146).

verses.zh: 折脚折手的、
verses.en: or a man who has had a broken leg or arm,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “who there is in him a broken leg or a broken arm,” or perhaps “broken foot or broken hand.” The Hebrew term רֶגֶל (regel) is commonly rendered “foot,” but it can also refer to the “leg,” and the Hebrew יָד (yad) is most often translated “hand,” but can also refer to the “[fore]arm” (as opposed to כַּף, kaf, “palm of the hand” or “hand”). See HALOT 386 s.v. יָד and 1184 s.v. רֶגֶל respectively (cf. the NJPS translation). In this context, these terms probably apply to any part of the limb that was broken, including hand and the foot. B. A. Levine (Leviticus [JPSTC], 146) points out that such injuries often did not heal properly in antiquity because they were not properly set and, therefore, remained a “physical flaw” permanently.

verses.zh: 驼背的、矮矬的、眼睛有毛病的、长癣的、长疥的，或是损坏肾子的，都不可近前来。
verses.en: or a hunchback, or a dwarf,[NOTE:1] or one with a spot in his eye,[NOTE:2] or a festering eruption, or a feverish rash,[NOTE:3] or a crushed testicle.
notes: Heb “thin”; cf. NAB “weakly.” This could refer to either an exceptionally small (i.e., dwarfed) man (B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 146) or perhaps one with a “withered limb” (J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 342, 344).

The term rendered “spot” derives from a root meaning “mixed” or “confused” (cf. NAB “walleyed”). It apparently refers to any kind of marked flaw in the eye that can be seen by others. Smr, Syriac, Tg. Onq., and Tg. Ps.-J. have plural “his eyes.”

The exact meaning and medical reference of the terms rendered “festering eruption” and “feverish rash” is unknown, but see the translations and remarks in B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 146; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 342, 344, 349-50; and R. K. Harrison, NIDOTTE 1:890 and 2:461.

verses.zh: 祭司亚伦的后裔，凡有残疾的，都不可近前来，将火祭献给耶和华。他有残疾，不可近前来献　神的食物。
verses.en: No man from the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a physical flaw may step forward[NOTE:1] to present the Lord’s gifts; he has a physical flaw, so he must not step forward to present the food of his God.
notes: Or “shall approach” (see HALOT 670 s.v. נגשׁ).

verses.zh: 神的食物，无论是圣的，至圣的，他都可以吃。
verses.en: He may eat both the most holy and the holy food of his God,

verses.zh: 但不可进到幔子前，也不可就近坛前；因为他有残疾，免得亵渎我的圣所。我是叫他成圣的耶和华。」
verses.en: but he must not go near the special curtain[NOTE:1] or step forward to the altar because he has a physical flaw. Thus[NOTE:2] he must not profane my holy places, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.’”
notes: See the note on Lev 16:2 for information on the curtain.
Heb “And.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here.

verses.zh: 于是，摩西晓谕亚伦和亚伦的子孙，并以色列众人。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] Moses spoke these things[NOTE:2] to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites.
notes: Heb “And.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) introduces a concluding statement for all the preceding material.
The words “these things” are not in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied in the translation for clarity.
